people.label: Jacob
people.b: Patriarch, son of Isaac, father of twelve tribes
people.s: Israel, also named Jacob, was the son of Isaac, the father of the twelve tribes of Israel, and a key patriarch of the Jewish people.

people.label: Jesus
people.b: The Son of God and Savior of the world.
people.s: Jesus Christ, the central figure of Christianity, is the Son of God who became incarnate, died for the sins of humanity, and rose from the dead, providing salvation for all who believe in Him.

people.label: Judah
people.b: Israelite tribe, kingdom, and province
people.s: Judah, also known as the Jews or Judea, refers to the Israelite tribe, the southern kingdom, and the Roman province in various biblical contexts.

people.label: David
people.b: Anointed king of Israel, ancestor of Jesus Christ
people.s: David, son of Jesse, was the anointed king of Israel, a man after God's own heart, and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.

people.label: Moses
people.b: Prophet who led Israel out of Egypt
people.s: Moses was a prophet whom God used to lead Israel out of slavery in Egypt and give them the law.

people.label: Aaron
people.b: Moses' brother, first high priest of Israel
people.s: Aaron was Moses' older brother and served as the first high priest of Israel.

people.label: Saul
people.b: First king of Israel, anointed by Samuel
people.s: Saul was the first king of Israel, anointed by the prophet Samuel, who initially followed God but later disobeyed and was rejected as king.

people.label: Abraham
people.b: Patriarch, chosen by God to father His people
people.s: Abraham, originally named Abram, was the patriarch whom God called to leave his homeland and blessed to become the father of many nations, establishing His covenant with him and his descendants.

people.label: Solomon
people.b: Son of David, king of Israel, known for his wisdom.
people.s: Solomon, also called Jedidiah, was the son of David and Bathsheba who succeeded his father as king of Israel and was renowned for his wisdom, wealth, and the construction of the First Temple in Jerusalem.

people.label: Joseph of Egypt
people.b: Son of Jacob, ruler in Egypt
people.s: Joseph, Jacob's son, rose to power in Egypt and saved his family during a famine.

people.label: Joshua
people.b: Moses' assistant who led Israel into Canaan
people.s: Joshua, the son of Nun, was Moses' assistant and successor who led the Israelites into the Promised Land.

people.label: Paul
people.b: Apostle to the Gentiles, author of many NT epistles
people.s: Paul, also known as Saul, the apostle to the Gentiles and author of many New Testament epistles.

people.label: Peter
people.b: Apostle of Jesus, leader in the early church
people.s: Peter, also known as Simon, Cephas, or Simon Bar-Jonah, was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus and a prominent leader in the early Christian church.

people.label: Benjamin
people.b: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel
people.s: Benjamin, initially named Ben-oni by his mother Rachel, was the youngest son of Jacob.

people.label: Jeremiah
people.b: Son of Hilkiah, the prophet during Judah's final days.
people.s: Jeremiah, the son of Hilkiah, was a prophet who ministered during the reigns of the last kings of Judah, warning of the Babylonian exile and calling for repentance.

people.label: Isaac
people.b: Son of Abraham; father of Jacob and Esau.
people.s: Isaac was the son of Abraham and Sarah, and the father of Jacob and Esau. God made a covenant with him, renewing the promises given to Abraham.

people.label: Samuel
people.b: Prophet and last judge of Israel before the kings
people.s: Samuel was a prophet and the last judge of Israel before the establishment of the monarchy, who anointed both Saul and David as kings.

people.label: Hezekiah
people.b: A righteous king of Judah.
people.s: Hezekiah was a king of Judah who instituted religious reforms and trusted in God during the Assyrian invasion.

people.label: Absalom
people.b: David's rebellious son who tried to usurp the throne.
people.s: Absalom was David's third son who led a revolt against his father's reign.

people.label: Elijah
people.b: A prophet during the reigns of Ahab and Ahaziah.
people.s: Elijah was a prominent prophet in Israel during the reigns of Ahab and Ahaziah, known for his miracles and confrontations with the prophets of Baal.

people.label: John the Baptist
people.b: The Baptist, a prophet who prepared the way for Jesus
people.s: John the Baptist was a prophet who preached repentance and baptized many, including Jesus, preparing the way for the Messiah.

people.label: Nebuchadnezzar
people.b: Emperor of Babylon who conquered Judah
people.s: Nebuchadnezzar II was the powerful Emperor of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem and exiled the Jews.

people.label: Reuben
people.b: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah
people.s: Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob and Leah, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

people.label: Esau
people.b: Isaac's firstborn son; sold birthright to Jacob; became Edom.
people.s: Esau, also called Edom, was Isaac's firstborn son who sold his birthright to his twin brother Jacob and became the father of the Edomites.

people.label: Jonathan
people.b: Eldest son of King Saul and friend of David
people.s: Jonathan, the eldest son of King Saul, was a valiant warrior and a close friend of David, ultimately dying in battle alongside his father.

people.label: Jeroboam I
people.b: First king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
people.s: Jeroboam I was the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the split of the united monarchy following Solomon's reign.

people.label: Ahab
people.b: Wicked king of Israel; husband of Jezebel
people.s: Ahab, son of Omri, reigned as king of Israel and did evil in the sight of the Lord.

people.label: Daniel
people.b: Prophet in Babylon, known for wisdom and visions
people.s: Daniel, also called Belteshazzar, was a prophet in Babylon known for his wisdom, integrity, and interpretation of dreams and visions.

people.label: Isaiah
people.b: Prophet during reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah.
people.s: Isaiah was a prophet in Judah during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. His prophecies are recorded in the biblical book bearing his name.

people.label: Zedekiah
people.b: Last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile
people.s: Zedekiah, originally named Mattaniah, was the last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile.

people.label: Elisha
people.b: A prophet who succeeded Elijah.
people.s: Elisha was a prophet who performed many miracles and served as a spiritual leader in Israel after Elijah.

people.label: Job
people.b: A righteous man who endured great suffering
people.s: Job, a blameless and upright man from Uz, endured severe trials and maintained his faith in God.

people.label: Pontius Pilate
people.b: Roman governor who presided over Jesus' trial
people.s: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea who presided over the trial of Jesus and ultimately ordered his crucifixion.

people.label: Gideon
people.b: Judge of Israel; defeated Midianites; tested and reassured by God.
people.s: Gideon, also called Jerubbaal or Jerubbesheth, was a judge of Israel who, with God's help, defeated the Midianites and delivered Israel from oppression.

people.label: Mordecai
people.b: Esther's cousin, a Jewish leader in the Persian court.
people.s: Mordecai, Esther's cousin and guardian, played a crucial role in saving the Jews from Haman's plot during the reign of King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) of Persia.

people.label: Josiah
people.b: King of Judah known for his religious reforms
people.s: Josiah was a king of Judah who instituted significant religious reforms and repaired the temple.

people.label: Sarah
people.b: Wife of Abraham; mother of Isaac
people.s: Sarah (or Sarai) was the wife of Abraham and the mother of Isaac, through whom God fulfilled His promise to make Abraham a great nation.

people.label: Noah
people.b: Righteous man, built ark, survived flood
people.s: Noah was a righteous man who built the ark and survived the great flood with his family.

people.label: Jehu
people.b: Son of Jehoshaphat, king of Israel, destroyed Ahab's dynasty.
people.s: Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, was anointed king of Israel by Elisha's servant; he destroyed the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal, but continued in the sins of Jeroboam.

people.label: Laban
people.b: Brother of Rebekah; father of Leah and Rachel
people.s: Laban, the brother of Rebekah and father of Jacob's wives, Leah and Rachel.

people.label: Esther
people.b: Jewish queen of Persia; saved her people from genocide.
people.s: Esther, also known as Hadassah, was a Jewish queen of Persia who saved her people from genocide.

people.label: Haman
people.b: A Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.
people.s: Haman, a high-ranking Persian official, conspired to kill all the Jews in the empire but was ultimately thwarted by Queen Esther and Mordecai.

people.label: Rachel
people.b: Wife of Jacob; mother of Joseph and Benjamin
people.s: Rachel was the beloved wife of Jacob, and the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.

people.label: Jesse
people.b: Father of King David.
people.s: Jesse was the father of King David and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.

people.label: Rehoboam
people.b: Son of Solomon, first king of Judah
people.s: Rehoboam was the son of Solomon and the first king of Judah after the division of the kingdom.

people.label: Samson
people.b: Israelite judge with great strength from God
people.s: Samson was an Israelite judge known for his God-given strength, which he used to fight against the Philistines.

people.label: John (son of Zebedee)
people.b: Apostle and son of Zebedee
people.s: John and James, the sons of Zebedee, were among the twelve apostles and part of Jesus' inner circle.

people.label: Lot
people.b: Abraham's nephew; rescued from Sodom's destruction
people.s: Lot, the nephew of Abraham, was rescued from Sodom before its destruction.

people.label: Leah
people.b: Wife of Jacob; mother of six sons and Dinah
people.s: Leah, the first wife of Jacob and mother of six of his sons and his daughter Dinah.

people.label: Eli
people.b: High priest and judge of Israel at Shiloh
people.s: Eli was the high priest and judge of Israel who ministered at the tabernacle in Shiloh.

people.label: Nathan (prophet)
people.b: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
people.s: Nathan, a prophet of God, served during the reigns of David and Solomon, offering guidance, confronting David's sin, and supporting Solomon's accession to the throne.

people.label: Rebekah
people.b: Wife of Isaac; mother of Jacob and Esau
people.s: Rebekah was the wife of Isaac and the mother of Jacob and Esau.

people.label: Xerxes
people.b: Persian Emperor (probably Xerxes I); husband of Esther
people.s: Ahasuerus, Emperor of Persia (probably Xerxes I), chose Esther as his queen and issued decrees impacting the Jews.

people.label: Caleb
people.b: Faithful spy, given Hebron as inheritance
people.s: Caleb, one of the twelve spies, remained faithful to God and was granted Hebron as his inheritance.

people.label: Barnabas
people.b: A Levite from Cyprus who accompanied Paul on missionary journeys.
people.s: Barnabas, also known as Joseph or Joses, was a Levite from Cyprus who played a significant role in the early church and accompanied Paul on missionary journeys.

people.label: Adam
people.b: The first man, created by God
people.s: Adam, the first man created by God, sinned and brought death into the world, but through Christ, the last Adam, came life and resurrection.

people.label: Ishmael son of Abraham
people.b: Son of Abraham and Hagar; father of Arab tribes.
people.s: Ishmael, the son of Abraham and Hagar, was the ancestor of various Arab tribes. Though not the chosen heir, he was still blessed by God.

people.label: Zerubbabel
people.b: Leader of the first Jewish exiles from Babylon
people.s: Zerubbabel, a descendant of David, led the first group of Jewish exiles back to Jerusalem from Babylon and oversaw the rebuilding of the temple.

people.label: Jephthah
people.b: A judge of Israel, known for his tragic vow.
people.s: Jephthah was a judge of Israel who delivered the Israelites from the Ammonites but made a tragic vow that resulted in the sacrifice of his daughter.

people.label: Herod Antipas
people.b: Tetrarch of Galilee during Jesus' ministry.
people.s: Herod Antipas was the tetrarch of Galilee during Jesus' ministry and played a role in Jesus' trial.

people.label: Jonah
people.b: Prophet swallowed by fish, preached to Nineveh
people.s: Jonah, a prophet from Gath-hepher, was sent to preach to Nineveh.

people.label: Manasseh (king)
people.b: King of Judah, son of Hezekiah.
people.s: Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, was a king of Judah who reigned for 55 years.

people.label: Timothy
people.b: Paul's young disciple and co-worker
people.s: Timothy was a young disciple and co-worker of Paul, who accompanied him on his missionary journeys and later served as a pastor.

people.label: Judas Iscariot
people.b: The apostle who betrayed Jesus
people.s: Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve apostles who betrayed Jesus, leading to His arrest and crucifixion.

people.label: Boaz
people.b: Kinsman-redeemer who married Ruth, ancestor of David and Jesus
people.s: Boaz, a wealthy Bethlehemite, married Ruth and became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

people.label: Ezra
people.b: Priest; scribe; led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem.
people.s: Ezra was a priest and scribe who led a group of Jewish exiles back to Jerusalem and played a key role in the spiritual reformation of the people.

people.label: Jezebel
people.b: Queen of Israel; wife of King Ahab
people.s: Queen Jezebel, the Phoenician wife of King Ahab, promoted Baal worship and persecuted the prophets of God.

people.label: Mary (mother of Jesus)
people.b: Mother of Jesus; wife of Joseph.
people.s: Mary, the mother of Jesus and wife of Joseph, was a virgin when she conceived by the Holy Spirit.

people.label: Naomi
people.b: Israelite woman, mother-in-law of Ruth.
people.s: Naomi, also known as Mara, was an Israelite woman who, after losing her husband and sons, returned from Moab to Bethlehem with her daughter-in-law Ruth.

people.label: Cyrus
people.b: Persian Emperor who decreed the rebuilding of the Temple
people.s: Cyrus, Emperor of Persia, issued a decree allowing the Jews to return and rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem.

people.label: James (son of Zebedee)
people.b: Son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve Apostles
people.s: James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, was one of the Twelve Apostles and a member of Jesus' inner circle.

people.label: Abednego
people.b: One of Daniel's companions, survived the fiery furnace
people.s: Azariah, also known as Abednego, was one of Daniel's companions who survived the fiery furnace (Dan.1.6, 7, 11, 19; 2:17, 49; 3).

people.label: Shadrach
people.b: One of Daniel's three friends in Babylon.
people.s: Hananiah, also known as Shadrach, was one of Daniel's three friends who were thrown into the fiery furnace for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image.

people.label: Meshach
people.b: A Jewish exile in Babylon, friend of Daniel.
people.s: Mishael, also known as Meshach, was one of the four young Jewish men chosen to serve in Nebuchadnezzar's court and was a companion of Daniel during the Babylonian exile.

people.label: Shem
people.b: Noah's son, ancestor of Semitic peoples
people.s: Shem, one of Noah's three sons and the ancestor of the Semitic peoples.

people.label: Silas
people.b: Prominent member of the Jerusalem church, companion of Paul.
people.s: Silas (or Silvanus) was a prominent member of the Jerusalem church who accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey and co-wrote some of his epistles.

people.label: Cain
people.b: Adam and Eve's firstborn son, killed his brother Abel
people.s: Cain, the firstborn son of Adam and Eve, murdered his brother Abel and was cursed by God to be a wanderer.

people.label: Joseph of Nazareth
people.b: Husband of Mary and earthly father of Jesus
people.s: Joseph was the husband of Mary and the earthly father of Jesus Christ.

people.label: Michal
people.b: Daughter of Saul; wife of David.
people.s: Michal, the younger daughter of King Saul, became David's wife and helped him escape from Saul's attempts to kill him.

people.label: Philip the apostle
people.b: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus
people.s: Philip, one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus, from Bethsaida in Galilee.

people.label: Artaxerxes
people.b: Persian king during Ezra and Nehemiah's time
people.s: Artaxerxes was the Persian king who allowed Ezra and Nehemiah to return to Jerusalem (Ezra 7:1,11-12,21; Neh.2.1; 5:14).

people.label: Mary Magdalene
people.b: Follower of Jesus, first witness of His resurrection.
people.s: Mary Magdalene, a follower of Jesus, was the first to witness His resurrection.

people.label: Barak
people.b: An Israelite commander who defeated Canaanite forces with Deborah.
people.s: Barak, son of Abinoam, led the Israelites to victory against Canaanite forces under Deborah's leadership.

people.label: Abigail
people.b: Wife of Nabal, later married David
people.s: Abigail, initially the wife of Nabal, became one of David's wives after Nabal's death and bore him a son named Chileab.

people.label: Ruth
people.b: Moabite woman, ancestor of David and Jesus
people.s: Ruth was a Moabite woman who married Boaz and became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

people.label: Andrew
people.b: Apostle, brother of Simon Peter
people.s: Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ and played a significant role in the early church.

people.label: Bathsheba
people.b: Wife of Uriah, later married David and bore Solomon.
people.s: Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, later became David's wife and the mother of Solomon.

people.label: Martha
people.b: Sister of Mary and Lazarus, hosted Jesus.
people.s: Martha, the sister of Mary and Lazarus, hosted Jesus in her home.

people.label: Miriam
people.b: Moses' sister, a prophetess who led women in worship.
people.s: Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron, was a prophetess who played a significant role in the Exodus and the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

people.label: Thomas
people.b: One of Jesus' twelve disciples, known for doubting
people.s: Thomas, also called Didymus, was one of Jesus' twelve disciples, known for doubting Jesus' resurrection until he saw him in person.

people.label: Haggai
people.b: A prophet who encouraged the rebuilding of the temple.
people.s: Haggai, a prophet during the post-exilic period, urged the people to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.

people.label: Hannah
people.b: The mother of the prophet Samuel.
people.s: Hannah, the wife of Elkanah, was the mother of the prophet Samuel, whom she dedicated to the Lord's service at a young age.

people.label: Herod the Great
people.b: The Great, Roman-appointed king of Judea during Jesus' birth.
people.s: Herod the Great was the Roman-appointed king of Judea who ruled during the time of Jesus' birth.

people.label: Lazarus
people.b: Brother of Mary and Martha; raised from the dead
people.s: Lazarus, the brother of Mary and Martha, was raised from the dead by Jesus (Jhn.11.1-44; 12.1-2,9-11).

people.label: Naaman
people.b: Aramean commander healed of leprosy by Elisha.
people.s: Naaman, a commander of the Aramean army, was healed of his leprosy by the prophet Elisha, demonstrating God's power and compassion.

people.label: Melchizedek
people.b: King of Salem and priest of God Most High.
people.s: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham.

people.label: Japheth
people.b: Son of Noah, ancestor of Indo-European peoples
people.s: Japheth was one of Noah's three sons and the ancestor of the Indo-European peoples.

people.label: Apollos
people.b: Eloquent Jewish Christian from Alexandria, co-worker with Paul
people.s: Apollos, an eloquent and learned Jewish Christian from Alexandria, was an important figure in the early church who worked alongside Paul in spreading the gospel.

people.label: Cornelius
people.b: Centurion, first Gentile convert to Christianity
people.s: Cornelius, a centurion, was the first Gentile convert to Christianity through Peter's ministry.

people.label: Enoch
people.b: A righteous man who walked with God.
people.s: Enoch, the son of Jared, walked with God and was taken by Him without experiencing death.

people.label: Mark
people.b: Barnabas's relative (KJV "sister's son", RV "cousin"); Paul's companion
people.s: Mark (also called John), a relative of Barnabas and Paul's companion, is traditionally named as the author of the Gospel of Mark.

people.label: Seth
people.b: Third son of Adam and Eve, ancestor of righteous line
people.s: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve, born after the death of Abel, and became the ancestor of the righteous line of humanity.

people.label: Barabbas
people.b: A notorious prisoner released instead of Jesus.
people.s: Barabbas, a notorious prisoner, was released by Pilate instead of Jesus at the crowd's demand.

people.label: Ham
people.b: One of Noah's three sons, father of Canaan.
people.s: Ham, one of Noah's three sons, was the father of Canaan and the ancestor of various nations.

people.label: Abel
people.b: Adam and Eve's second son, killed by Cain
people.s: Abel, the second son of Adam and Eve, was a shepherd who was killed by his brother Cain.

people.label: Deborah
people.b: Prophetess and judge who led Israel to victory over Canaanites.
people.s: Deborah, a prophetess and judge, led Israel to victory against the Canaanites alongside Barak.

people.label: Zechariah (priest)
people.b: Priest, father of John the Baptist
people.s: Zechariah, a priest of the division of Abijah, was the father of John the Baptist and husband of Elizabeth.

people.label: Belshazzar
people.b: The last Emperor of Babylon, son of Nabonidus.
people.s: Belshazzar, the last Emperor of Babylon, is mentioned in the book of Daniel as the son of Nebuchadnezzar (though historically known as the son of Nabonidus).

people.label: Darius the Mede
people.b: Mede who became Emperor over Babylon
people.s: Darius the Mede received the Empire of Babylon and ruled over it.

people.label: Ehud
people.b: Left-handed Benjamite judge who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression
people.s: Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, was a judge who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression by assassinating King Eglon and leading a victory over Moab.

people.label: Elizabeth
people.b: The wife of Zechariah and mother of John the Baptist.
people.s: Elizabeth was the wife of Zechariah, a priest, and the mother of John the Baptist.

people.label: Matthew
people.b: Apostle, tax collector, author of the Gospel of Matthew.
people.s: Matthew, also known as Levi, was a tax collector who became one of Jesus' twelve apostles and authored the Gospel of Matthew.

people.label: Rahab
people.b: A Canaanite woman who helped the Israelite spies in Jericho
people.s: Rahab, a Canaanite woman from Jericho, hid the Israelite spies and was spared during the city's destruction.

people.label: Amos
people.b: Prophet from Tekoa who prophesied to Israel
people.s: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, called by God as a prophet to Israel.

people.label: Methuselah
people.b: The oldest person mentioned in the Bible.
people.s: Methuselah, the son of Enoch, was the oldest person mentioned in the Bible, living 969 years.

people.label: Stephen
people.b: One of seven deacons, full of faith, performed miracles, martyred.
people.s: Stephen, one of the seven deacons chosen by the early church, was full of faith and the Holy Spirit, performed miracles, and became the first Christian martyr after his powerful testimony before the Sanhedrin.

people.label: Aquila
people.b: Jewish Christian tentmaker, co-worker with Paul
people.s: Aquila, along with his wife Priscilla, was a Jewish Christian who worked as a tentmaker and played a significant role in the early church, partnering with Paul in his ministry.

people.label: Goliath
people.b: A Philistine giant defeated by David.
people.s: Goliath was the Philistine champion from Gath who was defeated by David in a battle.

people.label: Priscilla
people.b: Early Christian teacher; wife of Aquila
people.s: Priscilla, also known as Prisca, was a Jewish Christian and the wife of Aquila, who worked with Paul in his ministry and hosted a church in their home.

people.label: Zechariah (prophet)
people.b: Post-exilic prophet who wrote the book of Zechariah
people.s: Zechariah, a post-exilic prophet and priest who wrote the book bearing his name.

people.label: Jael
people.b: Wife of Heber; killed Sisera, the Canaanite commander.
people.s: Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, killed Sisera, the commander of the Canaanite army, by driving a tent peg through his temple.

people.label: Delilah
people.b: Philistine woman who betrayed Samson
people.s: Delilah was a Philistine woman who deceived Samson into revealing the secret of his strength, leading to his capture.

people.label: Nathanael
people.b: Disciple of Jesus, from Cana in Galilee.
people.s: Nathanael, also known as Bartholomew, was one of Jesus' twelve disciples, who was initially skeptical but later confessed Jesus as the Son of God.

people.label: Joseph of Arimathea
people.b: Of Arimathea, buried Jesus in his own tomb
people.s: Joseph of Arimathea was a wealthy disciple who buried Jesus in his own new tomb.

people.label: Nehemiah
people.b: Governor of Judah, rebuilt Jerusalem's walls.
people.s: Nehemiah, the son of Hacaliah, served as the governor of Judah and led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls in the mid-5th century BC.

people.label: Nicodemus
people.b: Pharisee who visited Jesus
people.s: Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council who had several encounters with Jesus.

people.label: Eve
people.b: First woman; wife of Adam; tempted by the serpent.
people.s: Eve was the first woman, created as Adam's wife, who was tempted by the serpent and ate the forbidden fruit.

people.label: Hosea
people.b: A prophet to the northern kingdom of Israel.
people.s: Hosea was a prophet who ministered to the northern kingdom of Israel during the reigns of several kings, calling the people to repent and return to God.

people.label: Luke
people.b: Physician; companion of Paul; author of Luke and Acts
people.s: Luke, a physician and companion of Paul, was the author of the Gospel of Luke and the Book of Acts.

people.label: Zacchaeus
people.b: Tax collector who hosted Jesus in Jericho
people.s: Zacchaeus, a wealthy tax collector, hosted Jesus in his home and experienced a transformative encounter.

people.label: Ananias (husband of Sapphira)
people.b: Husband of Sapphira, lied about offering proceeds
people.s: Ananias, along with his wife Sapphira, lied to the apostles about the proceeds from the sale of their property and faced divine judgment.

people.label: Simon of Cyrene
people.b: A man who carried Jesus' cross on the way to crucifixion.
people.s: Simon of Cyrene was compelled by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus' cross on the way to his crucifixion.

people.label: Zipporah
people.b: Wife of Moses, daughter of Jethro
people.s: Zipporah, the daughter of Jethro, was Moses' wife and the mother of his two sons, Gershom and Eliezer.

people.label: Ezekiel
people.b: Prophet during Babylonian exile; author of the Book of Ezekiel.
people.s: Ezekiel was a prophet during the Babylonian exile who authored the Book of Ezekiel and served as a sign to the people of Israel.

people.label: Habakkuk
people.b: A prophet who questioned God's justice.
people.s: Habakkuk, a prophet, wrote the book bearing his name, which records his dialogue with God about justice and faith.

people.label: Joel (prophet)
people.b: A prophet of Judah and the author of the Book of Joel
people.s: Joel, the son of Pethuel, was a prophet of Judah who delivered a message of judgment and hope.

people.label: Lydia
people.b: Seller of purple goods; converted by Paul in Philippi
people.s: Lydia, a seller of purple goods from Thyatira, was converted by Paul in Philippi and hosted the church in her home.

people.label: Micah (prophet)
people.b: A prophet from Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.
people.s: Micah, a prophet from Moresheth, prophesied during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

people.label: Jairus
people.b: Synagogue leader whose daughter Jesus healed
people.s: Jairus, a synagogue leader, sought Jesus to heal his dying daughter.

people.label: Potiphar
people.b: Egyptian official who bought Joseph as a slave
people.s: Potiphar, the Egyptian officer who purchased Joseph as a slave and later imprisoned him after false accusations by Potiphar's wife.

people.label: Caesar Augustus
people.b: Roman emperor during the birth of Jesus
people.s: Augustus, also known as Caesar, was the Roman emperor during the time of Jesus' birth and early life (Luk.2.1).

people.label: Malachi
people.b: Prophet who wrote the book bearing his name.
people.s: Malachi, a prophet, received the word of the Lord to Israel.

people.label: Obadiah (prophet)
people.b: Prophet who prophesied against Edom
people.s: Obadiah was a prophet who delivered a message of judgment against the nation of Edom.

people.label: Sapphira
people.b: Wife of Ananias, lied to the apostles, died
people.s: Sapphira, along with her husband Ananias, lied to the apostles about the proceeds from a property sale and died as a result.

people.label: Bartimaeus
people.b: A blind beggar healed by Jesus near Jericho.
people.s: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was healed by Jesus as He was leaving Jericho.

people.label: Eutychus
people.b: Young man in Troas; fell from window; restored by Paul.
people.s: Eutychus was a young man in Troas who fell from a window and was restored to life by Paul.

people.label: Levi
people.b: Son of Jacob; progenitor of the Levites
people.s: Levi, son of Jacob and Leah, was the progenitor of the Levites, the priestly tribe of Israel.

people.label: Ephraim
people.b: Second son of Joseph, and a tribe of Israel.
people.s: Ephraim was the second son of Joseph, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel, often playing a prominent role in the nation's history.

people.label: Joab
people.b: Son of Zeruiah, commander of David's army
people.s: Joab, David's nephew and commander of his army, was a key figure in David's reign, known for his military prowess and loyalty.

people.label: Manasseh (son of Joseph)
people.b: Firstborn son of Joseph, blessed by Jacob.
people.s: Manasseh, Joseph's firstborn, was blessed by Jacob and became a tribe of Israel.

people.label: Pharaoh of the Exodus
people.b: Egyptian Pharaoh during the Exodus
people.s: Pharaoh, the Egyptian ruler who refused to release the Israelites from slavery, resulting in the ten plagues and the Exodus.

people.label: Pharaoh of Joseph's day
people.b: Egyptian ruler during Joseph's time
people.s: Pharaoh, the Egyptian ruler who elevated Joseph to a position of authority and welcomed his family to Egypt during a severe famine.

people.label: Jehoshaphat
people.b: Son of Asa, king of Judah.
people.s: Jehoshaphat was the son of Asa and became a powerful and righteous king of Judah.

people.label: Eleazar son of Aaron
people.b: Son of Aaron, high priest after his father
people.s: Eleazar was the son of Aaron and served as high priest after his father's death.

people.label: Balaam
people.b: A prophet hired to curse Israel but blessed them instead.
people.s: Balaam was a pagan prophet hired by Balak to curse Israel, but he blessed them instead.

people.label: Gad (son of Jacob)
people.b: Israelite tribe; descended from Gad, son of Jacob.
people.s: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from Gad, the son of Jacob, and known for their military prowess and settlement east of the Jordan River.

people.label: Abner
people.b: Saul's cousin and commander of his army
people.s: Abner, the son of Ner, was King Saul's cousin and the commander of his army; he later supported Saul's son Ish-bosheth as king before defecting to David.

people.label: Asa
people.b: King of Judah, son of Abijah; father of Jehoshaphat
people.s: Asa was a king of Judah who reigned for 41 years, known for his religious reforms (1Kings 15; 2Chr 14-16).

people.label: Naphtali
people.b: Son of Jacob, founder of the tribe of Naphtali.
people.s: Naphtali, the sixth son of Jacob and second son of Bilhah, was the founder of the Israelite tribe that bore his name.

people.label: Zebulun
people.b: Israelite tribe, son of Jacob and Leah
people.s: Zebulun was the tenth son of Jacob, the sixth and last of Leah, and his descendants formed one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

people.label: Asher
people.b: Son of Jacob and Zilpah, founder of the tribe of Asher
people.s: Asher was the eighth son of Jacob, born to Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, and became the founder of the tribe of Asher (Gen.30.13; 46:17; Deu.33:24; Jos.19:24-34; Luke 2.36).

people.label: Simeon (son of Jacob)
people.b: Son of Jacob and Leah, one of the twelve tribes.
people.s: Simeon, the second son of Jacob and Leah, was the founder of the tribe of Simeon and played a role in the story of Joseph.

people.label: Balak
people.b: King of Moab who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
people.s: Balak, son of Zippor, was the king of Moab who tried to curse Israel through Balaam.

people.label: Issachar
people.b: Son of Jacob and Leah, forefather of tribe
people.s: Issachar was the ninth son of Jacob and fifth by Leah, and he became the forefather of the Israelite tribe of Issachar.

people.label: Zadok the priest
people.b: High priest during the reigns of David and Solomon
people.s: Zadok was a prominent high priest who served during the reigns of King David and King Solomon.

people.label: Korah
people.b: Levite rebel leader; his descendants became temple servants
people.s: Korah, a Levite who rebelled against Moses and Aaron; his descendants became temple musicians and gatekeepers.

people.label: Abimelech son of Gideon
people.b: Son of Gideon, self-proclaimed king of Shechem
people.s: Abimelech, a son of Gideon, declared himself king of Shechem but was eventually killed when a millstone was dropped on his head during the siege of Thebez.

people.label: Ahaz
people.b: King of Judah, son of Jotham
people.s: Ahaz, son of Jotham, reigned as king of Judah for 16 years.

people.label: Jehoiakim
people.b: King of Judah, son of Josiah
people.s: Jehoiakim, also known as Eliakim, was a king of Judah who reigned for eleven years before being succeeded by his son Jehoiachin.

people.label: Amaziah
people.b: King of Judah, son of Joash
people.s: Amaziah, son of Joash, was the ninth king of Judah who reigned for 29 years.

people.label: Sihon
people.b: Amorite king of Heshbon, defeated by the Israelites.
people.s: Sihon was the Amorite king of Heshbon who refused to let the Israelites pass through his land and was subsequently defeated by them.

people.label: Asaph
people.b: Levite musician, psalmist, and ancestor of temple singers
people.s: Asaph was a Levite musician and psalmist during David's reign, and his descendants served as temple singers (1Ch.6.39; 15:17, 19; 16:5, 7, 37; 25:1, 2, 6, 9; 2Ch.5.12; 20:14; 29:13, 30; 35:15; Ezra 2:41; 3:10; Neh.7.44; 11:22; 12:35, 46; Psalms 50, 73-83).

people.label: Uzziah
people.b: King of Judah, reigned 52 years
people.s: Uzziah (Azariah) was king of Judah, known for his long and prosperous reign.

people.label: Abiathar
people.b: High priest during the reigns of David and Solomon
people.s: Abiathar, son of Ahimelech, was a high priest who served during the reigns of David and Solomon.

people.label: Ahaziah
people.b: King of Judah, son of Jehoram and Athaliah
people.s: Ahaziah (also called Jehoahaz), son of Jehoram, reigned as king of Judah for one year.

people.label: Baasha
people.b: Third king of Israel who ruled for 24 years.
people.s: Baasha, son of Ahijah, became king of Israel and reigned for 24 years.

people.label: Gedaliah
people.b: Appointed governor of Judah by Babylonians; assassinated by Ishmael.
people.s: Gedaliah, appointed governor of Judah by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem, was assassinated by Ishmael, leading to the flight of the remaining Jews to Egypt.

people.label: Jehoiada
people.b: High priest who overthrew Athaliah and crowned Joash
people.s: Jehoiada, also known as Barachiah, was a high priest who led a revolt against Queen Athaliah and crowned Joash as king of Judah.

people.label: Joash (king of Judah)
people.b: King of Judah, son of Ahaziah
people.s: Joash (Jehoash), son of Ahaziah, became king of Judah at age seven and reigned for forty years.

people.label: Abishai
people.b: David's nephew, one of his mighty men and commanders
people.s: Abishai, the son of Zeruiah and nephew of David, was a loyal commander and one of David's mighty men, known for his bravery and military prowess.

people.label: Adonijah
people.b: Son of David who attempted to seize the throne
people.s: Adonijah, the fourth son of David, declared himself king when David was old, but Solomon was chosen to succeed David instead, and Adonijah was later put to death for his rebellious actions.

people.label: Abimelech king of Gerar
people.b: Philistine king who interacted with Abraham and Isaac
people.s: Abimelech was a Philistine king who had dealings with both Abraham and Isaac, involving incidents where the patriarchs claimed their wives were their sisters.

people.label: Benaiah
people.b: Son of Jehoiada, a mighty warrior and loyal supporter of David and Solomon.
people.s: Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, was a mighty warrior in David's army and later served as the commander of Solomon's army and a key advisor to the king.

people.label: Hiram
people.b: King of Tyre, ally of David and Solomon.
people.s: Hiram, king of Tyre, provided materials and craftsmen for the construction of David's palace and Solomon's temple and palace.

people.label: Joash
people.b: King of Israel, son of Jehoahaz
people.s: Joash (Jehoash), son of Jehoahaz, reigned as king of Israel for sixteen years.

people.label: Og
people.b: King of Bashan, defeated by Israel
people.s: Og was the Amorite king of Bashan who was defeated by the Israelites during their journey to the Promised Land.

people.label: Uriah
people.b: Hittite soldier; husband of Bathsheba
people.s: Uriah was a Hittite soldier in David's army, the husband of Bathsheba, who was killed in battle as part of David's plan to cover up his adultery with Bathsheba.

people.label: Achish
people.b: Philistine king of Gath, gave refuge to David
people.s: Achish, also referred to as Abimelech, was the Philistine king of Gath who granted refuge to David when he fled from King Saul, but later dismissed him due to the suspicion of his servants.

people.label: Amnon
people.b: David's firstborn son, killed by Absalom
people.s: Amnon, David's firstborn son, raped his half-sister Tamar and was later killed by her brother Absalom.

people.label: Baruch
people.b: Jeremiah's scribe who recorded and delivered his prophecies.
people.s: Baruch, son of Neriah, served as Jeremiah's scribe and faithfully recorded and delivered his prophecies.

people.label: Hazael
people.b: King of Aram (Syria), anointed by Elijah.
people.s: Hazael, king of Aram, was anointed by Elijah and fought against Israel and Judah.

people.label: Ishmael who killed Gedaliah
people.b: Assassinated Gedaliah the governor; led captives to Ammon.
people.s: Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, assassinated Gedaliah the governor and led captives to Ammon before being pursued by Johanan.

people.label: Jehoiachin
people.b: King of Judah, son of Jehoiakim
people.s: Jehoiachin, also known as Jeconiah or Coniah, was a king of Judah who reigned for three months before being exiled to Babylon.

people.label: Jehoram
people.b: Son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
people.s: Jehoram, also known as Joram, was the son of Jehoshaphat and king of Judah.

people.label: Joshua (high priest)
people.b: High priest during the rebuilding of the temple
people.s: Joshua (or Jeshua), the son of Jehozadak, was the high priest who led the rebuilding of the temple after the Babylonian exile.

people.label: Abijah
people.b: King of Judah, son of Rehoboam
people.s: Abijah, the son of Rehoboam, reigned as king of Judah for three years and continued in the sins of his father.

people.label: Ithamar
people.b: Youngest son of Aaron; served as priest.
people.s: Ithamar was the fourth and youngest son of Aaron, who served as a priest alongside his brothers Nadab, Abihu, and Eleazar.

people.label: Jotham
people.b: King of Judah and son of Uzziah
people.s: Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was a king of Judah who reigned for sixteen years.

people.label: Joram
people.b: King of N. Israel, son of Ahab
people.s: Joram (or Jehoram), the son of Ahab, was king of Northern Israel for twelve years.

people.label: Hophra
people.b: Pharaoh during Jeremiah's time.
people.s: Hophra, also known as Pharaoh Apries, was the king of Egypt during the time of the prophet Jeremiah and the Babylonian invasion of Judah.

people.label: Micaiah
people.b: A prophet who foretold King Ahab's death.
people.s: Micaiah (or Micahu), a prophet, foretold the death of King Ahab of Israel in battle against the Arameans.

people.label: Nabal
people.b: Wealthy Carmelite; husband of Abigail. He was known for foolishness.
people.s: Nabal, a wealthy man from Carmel, was known for his foolishness and mistreatment of David, which nearly led to his demise.

people.label: Naboth
people.b: Jezreelite vineyard owner, unjustly killed by Ahab and Jezebel.
people.s: Naboth, a Jezreelite, was unjustly killed by King Ahab and Queen Jezebel for refusing to sell his ancestral vineyard.

people.label: Ben-hadad
people.b: King of Aram, contemporary of Asa and Baasha.
people.s: Ben-hadad I, king of Aram, made a treaty with Asa of Judah and attacked Israel during the reign of Baasha.

people.label: Sisera
people.b: Canaanite commander defeated by Deborah and Barak.
people.s: Sisera was the commander of the Canaanite army who was defeated by the Israelites under the leadership of Deborah and Barak.

people.label: Ahithophel
people.b: David's counselor who joined Absalom's rebellion, later committed suicide
people.s: Ahithophel was a wise counselor to David who defected to Absalom's side during Absalom's rebellion, but later committed suicide when his advice was not followed.

people.label: Darius the Great
people.b: Persian king who decreed the rebuilding of the Temple
people.s: Darius, king of Persia, issued a decree allowing the rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem.

people.label: Philip the evangelist
people.b: One of the seven deacons, evangelized in Samaria
people.s: Philip, one of the seven deacons chosen by the early church in Jerusalem, who preached the gospel in Samaria and baptized an Ethiopian eunuch.

people.label: Amon
people.b: King of Judah, son of Manasseh
people.s: Amon, the son of Manasseh, was the 15th king of Judah who reigned for two years before being assassinated by his servants.

people.label: Athaliah
people.b: Queen of Judah, daughter of Ahab
people.s: Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab, became queen of Judah and ruled for six years before being overthrown (2Ki.8.26; 11:1-3, 13-14, 20; 2Ch.22.2, 10-12; 23:12-13, 21; 24:7).

people.label: Jeduthun
people.b: Levitical musician and singer during David's reign
people.s: Jeduthun, also known as Ethan, was a Levitical musician and singer during the reign of King David.

people.label: Jehoahaz king of Israel
people.b: King of Israel, son of Jehu
people.s: Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, was king of Israel and reigned for seventeen years.

people.label: Jeroboam II
people.b: King of Israel, son of Jehoash.
people.s: Jeroboam II was a king of Israel who reigned for 41 years, restoring some of Israel's former territories.

people.label: Mephibosheth
people.b: Son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul.
people.s: Mephibosheth, also called Merib-baal, was the son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul.

people.label: Festus
people.b: Roman governor of Judea; heard Paul's case; sent him to Rome.
people.s: Porcius Festus succeeded Felix as the Roman governor of Judea and heard Paul's case, ultimately sending him to Rome for trial.

people.label: Gad the prophet
people.b: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
people.s: Gad was a prophet who advised King David and wrote a book of his acts.

people.label: Omri
people.b: King of Israel; father of Ahab
people.s: Omri was the sixth king of Israel who established Samaria as the capital and founded a powerful dynasty.

people.label: Sennacherib
people.b: Assyrian Emperor who invaded Judah
people.s: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, invaded Judah in the reign of King Hezekiah and besieged Jerusalem.

people.label: Tamar (David's daughter)
people.b: David's daughter, raped by her half-brother Amnon
people.s: Tamar was David's daughter who was raped by her half-brother Amnon, leading to tragic consequences.

people.label: King Agrippa
people.b: King who heard Paul's defense in Caesarea
people.s: King Agrippa heard Paul's defense and found no grounds for his imprisonment.

people.label: Hagar
people.b: Sarah's Egyptian maidservant; mother of Ishmael.
people.s: Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian maidservant, bore Abraham a son named Ishmael and is also mentioned in Paul's allegory in Galatians.

people.label: Heman
people.b: A Levite and chief musician in David's time.
people.s: Heman, a Levite, was a chief musician appointed by David to lead worship in the tabernacle.

people.label: Ish-bosheth
people.b: Son of Saul, king over Israel.
people.s: Ish-bosheth (also called Eshbaal), Saul's son, was made king over Israel by Abner but was ultimately assassinated, leading to David's rule over all Israel.

people.label: Tiberius
people.b: Roman emperor during Jesus' ministry and death
people.s: Tiberius was the Roman emperor during Jesus' ministry and crucifixion, mentioned in several Gospel accounts.

people.label: Titus
people.b: Gentile convert and companion of Paul
people.s: Titus was a Gentile convert and a trusted companion of Paul, who accompanied him on missionary journeys and served as his delegate to the church in Corinth.

people.label: Gehazi
people.b: Elisha's servant; punished with leprosy for greed and deceit.
people.s: Gehazi, the servant of the prophet Elisha, was punished with leprosy for his greed and deceit in the matter of Naaman's healing.

people.label: Hur
people.b: A companion of Moses and grandfather of Bezalel.
people.s: Hur was a prominent figure during the Israelites' journey in the wilderness, serving as a support to Moses and the grandfather of Bezalel, the chief artisan of the tabernacle.

people.label: Ahijah
people.b: Prophet from Shiloh who prophesied to Jeroboam
people.s: Ahijah the Shilonite was a prophet who foretold Jeroboam's rise to power and the division of the kingdom.

people.label: James brother of Jesus
people.b: Jesus' brother, leader in the Jerusalem church
people.s: James, the brother of Jesus, was a leader in the Jerusalem church and is traditionally named as the author of the epistle of James.

people.label: Jethro
people.b: Moses' father-in-law, priest of Midian
people.s: Jethro, also known as Reuel, was Moses' father-in-law and a priest of Midian.

people.label: Pekah
people.b: King of Israel who reigned for 20 years
people.s: Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel who reigned for 20 years.

people.label: Pharaoh, Solomon's father-in-law
people.b: Egyptian Pharaoh during Solomon's reign
people.s: Pharaoh, the Egyptian ruler who made an alliance with King Solomon and gave him his daughter in marriage.

people.label: Pharaoh who enslaved Israel
people.b: Egyptian Pharaoh during Moses' birth and early life
people.s: Pharaoh, the Egyptian ruler who oppressed the Israelites and decreed the killing of Hebrew male infants during the time of Moses' birth.

people.label: Zebedee
people.b: Father of the apostles James and John
people.s: Zebedee was the father of James and John, two of Jesus' twelve apostles, and was a fisherman by trade.

people.label: Mary of Bethany
people.b: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, sat at Jesus' feet.
people.s: Mary, the sister of Martha and Lazarus, sat at Jesus' feet and anointed Him with perfume.

people.label: Neco
people.b: Egyptian Pharaoh during the reigns of Josiah and Jehoiakim.
people.s: Pharaoh Neco II, the ruler of Egypt, opposed King Josiah of Judah, installed Jehoiakim as a vassal king, and was later defeated by Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

people.label: Nero
people.b: Roman emperor
people.s: Nero was likely the Roman emperor during Paul's final imprisonment.

people.label: Queen of Sheba
people.b: A queen who visited Solomon and praised his wisdom
people.s: The Queen of Sheba visited King Solomon, tested him with questions, and praised his wisdom and prosperity.

people.label: Terah
people.b: Abraham's father who settled in Haran
people.s: Terah was the father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, who left Ur to settle in Haran.

people.label: Vashti
people.b: Queen of Persia, deposed by King Ahasuerus (Xerxes)
people.s: Vashti, queen of Persia, was deposed by King Ahasuerus for disobeying his command.

people.label: Sanballat
people.b: Horonite leader who opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem
people.s: Sanballat the Horonite opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

people.label: Elkanah
people.b: The father of the prophet Samuel.
people.s: Elkanah was the father of the prophet Samuel and husband of Hannah.

people.label: Caiaphas
people.b: High priest during Jesus' ministry and trial
people.s: Caiaphas, the high priest during Jesus' ministry, presided over Jesus' trial and played a key role in His crucifixion.

people.label: Rezin
people.b: King of Aram (Syria) during the reign of Ahaz
people.s: Rezin was the king of Aram (Syria) who allied with Pekah, king of Israel, against Ahaz, king of Judah.

people.label: Tiglath-pileser
people.b: Assyrian king who conquered parts of Israel
people.s: Tiglath-pileser, widely identified with Pul, was an Assyrian king who conquered parts of Israel and received tribute from King Menahem.

people.label: Felix
people.b: Roman governor of Judea; heard Paul's case.
people.s: Felix was a Roman governor of Judea who heard the case against Paul and kept him in custody for two years.

people.label: Hananiah
people.b: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah's prophecies.
people.s: Hananiah, a false prophet, opposed Jeremiah's prophecies and falsely predicted the end of the Babylonian captivity within two years.

people.label: Hoshea
people.b: The last king of Israel (northern kingdom).
people.s: Hoshea was the last king of Israel, reigning from around 732 to 722 BC, until the Assyrian conquest of Samaria.

people.label: James son of Alphaeus
people.b: Apostle, son of Alphaeus; traditionally "James the Less"
people.s: James son of Alphaeus, traditionally known as "James the Less", was one of the Twelve Apostles.

people.label: Jehoahaz king of Judah
people.b: King of Judah, son of Josiah
people.s: Jehoahaz, also known as Johanan, was a king of Judah and the son of Josiah.

people.label: Menahem
people.b: King of Israel who reigned for ten years.
people.s: Menahem, king of Israel, known for his cruelty and for paying tribute to Assyria.

people.label: Zimri
people.b: King of Israel, reigned seven days
people.s: Zimri, a commander of half of Israel's chariots, became king after assassinating Elah, but his reign lasted only seven days.

people.label: Dinah
people.b: Daughter of Jacob and Leah
people.s: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, was raped by Shechem, leading to a violent confrontation between her brothers and the Shechemites.

people.label: Bezalel
people.b: Skilled craftsman who built the tabernacle
people.s: Bezalel, son of Uri, was a skilled craftsman filled with God's Spirit to build the tabernacle and its furnishings.

people.label: Uzzah
people.b: Died while moving the ark; place named after him
people.s: Uzzah died while moving the ark; the place was named Perez-uzzah.

people.label: Tamar (Judah's daughter-in-law)
people.b: Judah's daughter-in-law who bore Perez and Zerah
people.s: Tamar was Judah's daughter-in-law who, after being wronged by him, bore twin sons Perez and Zerah.

people.label: Achan
people.b: An Israelite who stole devoted things, causing Israel's defeat.
people.s: Achan took devoted things, leading to Israel's defeat at Ai.

people.label: Herod Agrippa I
people.b: A king who persecuted the early church.
people.s: Herod Agrippa I was a king who persecuted the early church, killing James and imprisoning Peter.

people.label: Herodias
people.b: Wife of Herod Antipas who had John beheaded.
people.s: Herodias was the wife of Herod Antipas, who had John the Baptist beheaded at her request.

people.label: Othniel
people.b: First judge of Israel, Caleb's nephew
people.s: Othniel, Caleb's nephew, was the first judge of Israel who delivered the people from Cushan-Rishathaim.

people.label: Eliphaz
people.b: A Temanite, one of Job's three friends.
people.s: Eliphaz the Temanite was one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him during his affliction.

people.label: Elimelech
people.b: Naomi's husband from Bethlehem.
people.s: Elimelech was Naomi's husband from Bethlehem who died in Moab.

people.label: Obed
people.b: Son of Boaz and Ruth
people.s: Obed was the son of Boaz and Ruth, and the grandfather of King David.

people.label: Ebed-melech
people.b: Ethiopian eunuch who rescued Jeremiah from a cistern
people.s: Ebed-melech, an Ethiopian eunuch in King Zedekiah's service, rescued the prophet Jeremiah from a cistern and was promised safety by God for his faith.

people.label: Thaddaeus
people.b: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus
people.s: Judas, also known as Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus, was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus Christ.

people.label: Bildad
people.b: One of Job's three friends
people.s: Bildad the Shuhite was one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him during his affliction.

people.label: Ananias of Damascus
people.b: Disciple in Damascus, baptized Saul (Paul)
people.s: Ananias, a disciple in Damascus, was sent by God to heal and baptize Saul (later known as Paul) after his conversion on the road to Damascus.

people.label: Hophni
people.b: A corrupt priest, son of Eli.
people.s: Hophni, along with his brother Phinehas, was a corrupt priest who served under his father Eli at the tabernacle in Shiloh.

people.label: Bartholomew
people.b: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ.
people.s: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.

people.label: Onesimus
people.b: Runaway slave, convert of Paul
people.s: Onesimus was a runaway slave who became a Christian through Paul's ministry and was the subject of Paul's letter to Philemon.

people.label: Simon the Zealot
people.b: One of the twelve apostles, also called the Zealot.
people.s: Simon, also known as the Zealot, was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.

people.label: Zophar
people.b: One of Job's three friends, the Naamathite
people.s: Zophar the Naamathite was one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him during his affliction.

people.label: Eglon
people.b: King of Moab who oppressed Israel
people.s: Eglon, king of Moab, oppressed Israel for 18 years until Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, assassinated him and delivered Israel.

people.label: Nimrod
people.b: Mighty hunter, built cities
people.s: Nimrod was a mighty hunter and ruler who built several notable cities, including Babel and Nineveh.

people.label: Simon the sorcerer
people.b: Sorcerer in Samaria who tried to buy the Holy Spirit's power.
people.s: Simon was a sorcerer in Samaria who believed and was baptized but later tried to buy the power of the Holy Spirit from the apostles.

people.label: Epaphras
people.b: A faithful minister and fellow servant of Paul.
people.s: Epaphras was a faithful minister of Christ and a fellow prisoner with Paul, who labored in prayer for the Colossians.

people.label: Jude brother of Jesus
people.b: A brother of Jesus and author of the epistle
people.s: Jude, a brother of Jesus, was the author of the Epistle of Jude and is mentioned in the lists of Jesus' siblings.

people.label: Dorcas
people.b: Charitable woman in Joppa whom Peter raised from the dead
people.s: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was a beloved disciple in Joppa known for her charitable works, whom Peter raised from the dead.

people.label: Salome (at the cross)
people.b: Witness of Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection
people.s: Salome was one of the women who witnessed Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection. She was perhaps the wife of Zebedee.

people.label: Agabus
people.b: Prophet who predicted famine and Paul's arrest
people.s: Agabus, a prophet, foretold a famine and Paul's arrest in Jerusalem.

people.label: Gamaliel
people.b: Pharisee; teacher of the law; Paul's mentor.
people.s: Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee and teacher of the law, was Paul's mentor and advised the Sanhedrin to be cautious in their treatment of the apostles.

people.label: Huldah
people.b: A prophetess during the reign of King Josiah.
people.s: Huldah was a prophetess who was consulted by King Josiah's officials regarding the authenticity of the Book of the Law discovered during temple repairs.

people.label: Matthias
people.b: Apostle chosen to replace Judas Iscariot.
people.s: Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot as one of the twelve apostles.

people.label: Philemon
people.b: Recipient of Paul's letter, Colossian slave owner
people.s: Philemon, a Christian from Colossae to whom Paul wrote a letter appealing for the reconciliation with his runaway slave, Onesimus.

people.label: Simeon who held baby Jesus
people.b: Righteous and devout man who blessed Jesus in the temple.
people.s: Simeon was a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem who blessed the infant Jesus in the temple and prophesied about his future.

people.label: Orpah
people.b: Naomi's daughter-in-law, stayed in Moab
people.s: Orpah was Naomi's daughter-in-law who stayed in Moab after the death of her husband, while Ruth accompanied Naomi to Bethlehem.

people.label: Aeneas
people.b: Paralyzed man in Lydda healed by Peter
people.s: Aeneas, paralyzed for eight years, was healed by Peter in Lydda.

people.label: Jochebed
people.b: Mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
people.s: Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, married her nephew Amram and became the mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

people.label: Peninnah
people.b: Elkanah's wife, rival of Hannah
people.s: Peninnah, one of Elkanah's two wives and the rival of Hannah, Samuel's mother.

people.label: Phoebe
people.b: Deacon of the church in Cenchreae
people.s: Phoebe, a deacon of the church in Cenchreae, whom Paul commended to the believers in Rome.

people.label: Joanna
people.b: A follower of Jesus who supported His ministry
people.s: Joanna, the wife of Chuza, was one of the women who followed and supported Jesus during His earthly ministry.

people.label: Anna
people.b: Prophetess who witnessed Jesus' dedication in the temple
people.s: Anna, a prophetess and widow, witnessed the dedication of the infant Jesus in the temple and spoke about Him to all who were looking forward to the redemption of Jerusalem.

people.label: Eunice
people.b: Mother of Timothy; a Jewish believer.
people.s: Eunice was the mother of Timothy and a Jewish believer.

people.label: Lois
people.b: Grandmother of Timothy; commended for her faith
people.s: Lois, the grandmother of Timothy, was commended by Paul for her sincere faith.

people.label: Nahum
people.b: Old Testament prophet, author of the Book of Nahum.
people.s: Nahum, identified as the Elkoshite, was a prophet of God who delivered a message of judgment against the Assyrian city of Nineveh.

people.label: Zephaniah
people.b: Prophet, son of Cushi, descendant of Hezekiah
people.s: Zephaniah, the prophet who wrote the book bearing his name, was the son of Cushi and descendant of Hezekiah.

people.label: Rhoda
people.b: Servant girl in the house of Mary
people.s: Rhoda was a servant girl in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark, who recognized Peter's voice at the door.

people.label: Malchus
people.b: High priest's servant whose ear was cut off by Peter.
people.s: Malchus, the high priest's servant, had his ear cut off by Peter during Jesus' arrest.
